resources.string: Pupillary distance in under a minute
We will take a picture of your face with the front camera, then measure pupillary distance.
You should have a standard size card, like a credit card or an ID card.
Place and hold the card flat on your forehead, just above your eyes.
Hold the phone at least 6 inches (15 cm) away.
Those markers could not be measured. Drag both points apart and try again.
The front camera takes one picture of your face. From that photo we measure the distance between your pupils.
Bring a card you already have
A credit card, debit card, or ID works. Its standard width is the ruler the measurement is based on.
Hold the card flat on your forehead, long edge horizontal, just above your brows. Keep the full card in frame.
Hold the phone about 15 cm (6 in) away, look straight ahead, and use even light so both eyes stay sharp.
Line both eyes up inside the oval.
Rest the card flat on your forehead.
Hold the phone about 15 cm away.
Face a window or a soft light, then look straight ahead.
Tap the shutter when the card and both eyes sit inside the guide.
Check that the card edges and both pupils are sharp.
The measurement needs a live preview so you can line up the card before the shutter fires.
Camera access is required to photograph the card and your eyes.
The photo did not save. Try the shutter again.
No camera is available on this device.
Drag the mint markers onto the center of each pupil. Pinch is not needed — just drop them in place.
Drag the amber markers to the two lower corners of the card. The line between them is the ruler.
Drag either marker. A light tap confirms the drop.
Measured from the card width in your photo. Use it when you order glasses.
